_readme: Explore photo + attribution backfill. Consumed by scripts/seed-explore-photos.mjs.
THIS FILE ADDS NO ROWS. Every entry UPDATEs an existing active `places` row by its
real UUID. The directory already holds 42 active places (38 landmarks, 4 beaches)
backfilled by 20260822_places_consolidation; 41 of them have no photo. The gap was
never missing places, it was missing photographs.
NO BEACHES HERE, DELIBERATELY. Beaches are live in production today (the Home
Beaches tile at App.js:1099 is NOT behind MODULE_FLAGS.explore), so a beach photo
renders immediately under the shipped credit-only renderer, which cannot show a
licence notice or link. Beach photos are therefore restricted to Unsplash/Pexels/own
— and no such photo exists: Unsplash and Pexels identify no named TRNC beach, and
every named-beach photo on Wikimedia Commons is CC BY-SA. Beaches wait for the
attribution renderer to reach production. The seed script enforces this as a hard
error, so re-adding a beach here fails the run rather than publishing quietly.
Landmarks ARE reachable in production today (search_content's landmark arm reads the
legacy `landmarks` table and HomeScreen.js:186 resolves the hit into this screen), so
the derived photo_credits string carries creator + licence + licence URI, not just a
name. See utils/photoAttribution.js legacyCreditString().
Per photo: credit, license, license_url, source_url are ALL required. The single
exemption is source:'own', which requires credit + license and whose source_url MUST
be null — and 'own' with a non-null source_url is equally an error, so the exemption
cannot be used to smuggle a photo past the check.

places.name: Kyrenia Castle
places._note: Provenance verified: the bucket file Kyrenia_Fortress_2.jpeg is Commons File:Kyrenia Fortress 2.JPG, and its artist + licence matched the photo_credits string already stored on the row. It was PRESERVED unresized in the first apply (2026-08-25) and re-mirrored immediately after, because at 2.4 MB it was ~5x the largest optimised photo and the only unoptimised image in the set. Its `src` is therefore OUR OWN bucket object, not Commons: the pixels are already ours, so re-fetching from Commons would be a pointless round trip. Kyrenia_Fortress_2.jpeg is NOT deleted — the saved rollback block for the first apply references it and must keep resolving. source_url still points at the Commons file page, which is where the licence and creator live.
